metadata.title: A Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Ramp Metering Based on Traffic Video Data
supplementary_materials: data available from corresponding author upon request

metadata.hardware_requirements: computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic flow data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, used for simulation calibration and evaluation in SUMO.
nodes_source.size_estimate: 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: The paper explicitly states that the data used to support the results are available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extract vehicle coordinates (xi, yi) from raw video frames within a control area of size X x Y and map them to position matrices mt where cells occupied by vehicles are set to constant UV.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st.
nodes_process.description: Perform zooming and down-sampling on position matrices to reduce dimensions. Stack N consecutive matrices to capture traffic dynamics. Incorporate previous signal state into the matrix.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, 0/2 tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: Train a multi-branch CNN using Deep Q-Learning with experience replay and a target network. Use multitask learning to simultaneously predict Q-values, mean speed, and queue length.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all tools named, all parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator.
nodes_process.description: Evaluate the DRL policy against no-control and PI-ALINEA baselines in a freeway merge scenario. Metrics include travel time, queue length, speed, and downstream flow over 20 simulations.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, tool named (version missing), parameters stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Divide the control area into 8 subareas. Systematically remove information from specific subareas in the input data to observe the impact on travel time metrics.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence plots of episode reward and mean travel time over one million training frames, demonstrating learning stability.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: RL parameters and Algorithm 1 specified; raw demand and initial network weights missing.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9: Vehicle travel times in the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Mainline travel times (Q1, Q2, Q3) comparing no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL strategies over 70 minutes.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: SUMO configuration detailed; results based on 20 seeds; demand profile summarized in text.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2: Mean travel times in 20 simulation experiments (s).
nodes_sink.description: Comparison of mean vehicle travel times across 20 experiments for no-control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Specific numerical outcomes for 20 simulation runs provided; methods and setup mostly specified.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10: Temporal-spatial distribution of speed in (a) no-control; (b) PI-ALINEA; (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Spatial-temporal heatmaps of traffic speeds along the mainline for three different control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visualization directly derived from reported evaluation simulation metrics.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11: Queue length at the on-ramp.
nodes_sink.description: Quantile plots of on-ramp vehicle queue lengths for three control strategies over the evaluation period.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Standard simulation metric produced by the described evaluation methodology.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12: Relationship of queue length and red ratio for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plots with regression lines showing the relationship between signal red ratio and average queue length.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Aggregates data from 20 simulation experiments for each control method.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13: Queue length and occupancy for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Temporal correlation plots between on-ramp queue length and mainline occupancy for two methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visual comparison of time-series metrics produced by the core simulation study.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots showing the distribution of downstream traffic volumes across different time steps.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Simulation outcome; consistent with reported capacity drop alleviation claims.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16: Travel time with perturbed input data.
nodes_sink.description: Sensitivity analysis box plots for mainline travel times under data occlusion for eight subareas.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Perturbation methodology and subarea division clearly described in text.
